subject: Post-demo: procurement readiness & payment routing for StrataGen
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron@stratagen.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: procurement readiness & payment routing for StrataGen

Aaron — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so procurement has what they need to move forward.

Summary of demo: Redwood Dedicated for clinical-inference pilot, model pinned to rdx-gpt-13b, expected steady-state 50 qps with bursts to 200 for batch jobs. Key asks you mentioned: PO for production, ability to start pilot on card, SOC2 evidence, and an option to go through AWS Marketplace if it helps procurement.

Procurement / AP questions we discussed (what we need from you):
- Confirm who in your AP team will run vendor onboarding (name + email).
- Which payment path is preferred for production: PO (net-30/45) or corporate card? If PO, is a standard purchase order sufficient or do you require a signed SOW + PO?
- Any vendor onboarding docs we should expect (W9, Insurance cert, vendor questionnaire).

Attachments I’m sharing in this thread: SOW_StrataGen_v1.1.pdf (pilot scope + pricing), vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx, procurement_faqs.md — these cover our typical onboarding timeline and the minimum fields your AP team will ask for.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm AP contact and preferred payment path (PO vs card) — Aaron
2) If card for pilot: provision a trial card and we proceed to setup (we can start in 3 business days).
3) If PO for pilot: we’ll need signed SOW + PO; expected vendor onboarding 10–15 business days if your AP has standard intake.
4) I’ll introduce you to Marissa from RevOps to help with any exceptions or temporary card-based pilots.

If helpful, we can also pursue an AWS Marketplace listing for procurement to buy via marketplace contract — that sometimes shortens vendor intake.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call with procurement if that helps speed things up.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Aaron Li <aaron@stratagen.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Green <samantha@stratagen.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement readiness & payment routing for StrataGen

Thanks Ben — good recap. A few clarifications from our side after an initial sync with AP:

- Our procurement team strongly prefers PO for any production spend. For pilots under $25k we can sometimes accept a card, but only if RevOps or Finance signs off on a temporary exception.
- AP will require a vendor questionnaire (we’ll send our standard form), a completed W9, and proof of insurance.
- We do have an internal policy that vendors must accept net-45 for larger deals — is Redwood able to accept net-45 on annual contracts, or do you require net-30?
- Marketplace: purchasing via AWS Marketplace helps our procurement team because they can route through our AWS consumption budget. Would Redwood be open to that pathway if it reduces friction?

I’m looping in Samantha from procurement — she’ll own vendor intake. Samantha, can you confirm the vendor questionnaire timing and whether StrataGen can run an initial pilot on card while onboarding completes?

Appreciate it — Aaron

Aaron Li
Head of ML Infrastructure | StrataGen Therapeutics
aaron@stratagen.ai | +1 617-555-0246
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron@stratagen.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement readiness & payment routing for StrataGen

Aaron / Samantha — great, thanks for the rapid follow-up. Answers inline: 

- Net terms: We can accept net-45 on annual commitments with a credit review and an enterprise payment addendum (we’ll flag this to Legal). For pilots, standard is immediate payment (card) or pre-paid invoice; we don’t force net-30 for pilot-only consumption.
- Marketplace: yes — we can route via AWS Marketplace for billing; that typically reduces procurement friction but does add a slight margin difference on our side. If your team prefers marketplace procurement we can expedite that track.
- Onboarding docs: attaching vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx and procurement_faqs.md. W9 and insurance cert we can provide immediately.

Suggested path for minimal friction (pilot -> scale):
1) Pilot: start on corporate card (one-month pilot) while vendor onboarding is processed in parallel. This keeps timeline shortest (we can spin up in 48–72 hours once we have a card).
2) Production: sign SOW + PO and migrate billing to net-45 under the enterprise terms.

If procurement needs an interim approval, Marissa (cc’d) can submit a one-time pilot exception to Finance so the card route is formally approved; otherwise AP will need a PO up-front.

Docs attached: SOW_StrataGen_v1.1.pdf (pilot pricing), vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx, procurement_faqs.md

Next step: Samantha — can you confirm whether StrataGen will issue a card for the month-one pilot, or if you prefer we go the SOW+PO route? If you want, I’ll send a short DocuSign for the SOW to speed signing.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

Attachments: SOW_StrataGen_v1.1.pdf (36KB), vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (12KB), procurement_faqs.md (8KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: AP constraints and exception playbook for StrataGen (FYI)

Ben / Marissa — quick internal note summarizing options so we’re aligned before we respond to procurement: 

Options (pros/cons):
- Card-first pilot (fastest): Pros = 48–72h start, minimal paperwork; Cons = needs Finance exception for pilot spend > $X or we accept on CC with limits. Requires formal approval from RevOps for one-time card usage.
- SOW + PO (default enterprise): Pros = clean for AP and legal, supports net-45; Cons = onboarding 10–15 business days, delays pilot start.
- Marketplace (AWS): Pros = procurement likes this, can use consumption budget; Cons = marketplace listing takes time on our side to finalize; margin impact on pricing.

I recommend we offer card-pilot + parallel onboarding and commit to a 10-business-day timeline for full onboarding if they choose PO for production. If procurement insists on PO-only even for pilot, escalate to Sales leadership for a temporary credit approval.

Marissa — can you prepare the pilot-exception template and a short note for Finance (we’ll need approximate pilot spend to justify)? Estimate pilot spend: $8,500 (one month).

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Green <samantha@stratagen.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement readiness & payment routing for StrataGen

Thanks team — quick update from procurement side:

- We can approve a corporate card for a limited one-month pilot up to $10k while vendor onboarding completes. That matches our internal policy and keeps timelines tight.
- We will still require the vendor questionnaire and W9; I’ll send the questionnaire today. Expect vendor intake to finish within 10 business days after we receive your completed checklist.
- For production, we will issue a PO (net-45) and need the signed SOW. Please proceed to send DocuSign for the SOW so our legal team can review in parallel.
- Marketplace is acceptable but not necessary for this pilot — keep that as a backup if we see vendor intake blocking acceptance.

Ben — please send the DocuSign link and the W9 to me; Marissa, if you can prepare the internal pilot exception note that would speed Finance approval.

Samantha Green
Procurement Manager | StrataGen Therapeutics
samantha@stratagen.ai | +1 617-555-0789
